newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - British Telecom gains.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - British Telecom gains.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc rose above a 12-month high Thursday to head British American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) following the Labour government's budget announcement.
Traders said British Telecom was among British ADRs seen as being helped by the budget, announced Wednesday, while dollar-sensitive exporters eased on the news.
"It was 'The Tale of Two Cities,'" a trader in British ADRs said. "The (overall) market's very strong, and all of the dollar earners have gotten crushed."
British Telecom was up 4-11/16 to 80-5/8, above a 12-month high. The ADR was among the percentage gainers on the New York Stock Exchange.

Analysts said the budget should help lift British Telecom's domestic earnings by 1.5 to two percent, excluding changes to pension fund tax credits. The company will be helped by installment payments of a windfall earnings tax and by a reduction in the corporate tax rate.
Other gainers included National Power Plc, which rose 3-1/16 to 38-11/16, and National Westminster Bank Plc, which was up 3-1/2 to 88-1/2. Both prices were 12-month highs.
The budget helped strengthen the pound, affecting the competitiveness of British exporters and depressing the value of their overseas earnings.
Among those affected, British Steel Plc fell 14/16 to 24-5/16 and Imperial Chemical Industries Plc fell 1-3/4 to 55-1/2.
Among active ADRs and foreign shares, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd rose 2/16 to 8-5/16 and Telefonos de Mexico was up 5/8 to a 12-month high of 50.
Swedish telecommunications equipment maker Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson rose 1-1/16 to 40-7/16.
The 814-strong ADR group was up 0.60 percent in late morning. ADRS allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
